messages:
jordan: Heads-up — noticed a perf regression on prod for short seqs (<64) when batching is tiny (1-4). Latency up ~20% on p4d nodes after the kernel selection tweak yesterday. perf-bot posted the CI trace: https://ci.internal/redwood/bug/4567 :thinking_face:

perf-bot: Regression detected: route=generate-hosted, model=rwft-7b, p99 latency +22% vs baseline. Diff at kernel selection stage. See /tmp/nvtx-trace-1783456789.json

kai: ugh, that's the small-batch path I changed to prefer the warp-specialized kernel for seqs <=128 to save smem on large batches. Might have missed reg for very small batch sizes. :grimacing:

sana: quick question — is this on the seq-dependent kernel path (i.e., kernel_picker(seq, batch) -> choice) or from batching heuristics changing effective batch distribution?

jordan: kernel picker. NVTX shows we switched from kernel_A_lowregs -> kernel_WarpSpec for many short requests. Kernel_WarpSpec uses more regs per thread (inlined fma) but lower shared memory per CTA. On p4d that increased register pressure and spilled in some warps => slower for tiny batches.

matt: can you paste the kernel pick table?

jordan: sure, snippet from the runtime trace: 
```
# simplified table (arch = p4d)
seq <= 64, batch >= 8 -> kernel_A_high_occ
seq <= 64, batch < 8 -> kernel_WarpSpec_low_smem  # chosen yesterday
64 < seq <= 256 -> kernel_WarpSpec
seq > 256 -> kernel_large_seq
```

lina: idea: WarpSpec wins when occupancy is limiting (large batch) because it reduces smem and enables more CTAs. For batch<8 we should probably prefer lower-reg kernel even if it uses more smem per CTA. Tradeoff is occupancy vs register spills.

kai: agreed. My intention was to bias toward smem-reducing kernels, forgot register footprint. On p4d registers per SM differ; kernel_WarpSpec compiled with -O3 inline increases regs by ~8.

sana: can we reproduce locally with microbench harness? I can run a matrix over seq=[16,32,64,128], batch=[1,2,4,8] for both kernels and collect metrics: achieved occupancy, committed_regs, spills, sm_efficiency, inst_issued. Also add nvprof counters: l2_hit_rate, stall_exec_dependency.

matt: also add per-thread stack spill counters and time-in-kernel with and without prefetch. If spills > 0 then effective latency jump expected.

jordan: ran quick perf capture on a dev p4d instance: kernel_WarpSpec for seq=32,batch=2 shows reg_alloc=64/thread, spills=3, achieved_occupancy=0.25. kernel_A_lowregs reg_alloc=56/thread, spills=0, occupancy=0.2 but end-to-end latency was lower. Means spills are killing us despite lower occupancy.

kai: ok patch proposal: modify picker for archs with smaller register file (or when compile_variant.regs > threshold) to prefer low-reg variant for batch < 8. Pseudocode:
```
if arch in {p4d, a100v1} and batch < 8 and seq <= 64:
  choose kernel_lowregs
else:
  choose kernel_warpspec_or_default
```

sana: +1 but let's add autotune datapoint: runtime should run a micro-benchmark on first cold node to pick between the two kernels for that arch+model combo and cache it for 12h. That avoids hardcoding thresholds.

lina: autotuner should measure: time_per_token, reg_spills, sm_efficiency, and choose the kernel that minimizes token-latency for the observed seq/batch distribution. Also store decision keyed by (arch, sm_version, model_variant, seq_bucket, batch_bucket).

matt: caution: running microbench at startup can add latency on scaleups. Make it async and use background trials with a brief canary percentage (1%) until decision stabilized.

jordan: for a hotfix let's change picker + add telemetry events so we can roll back quickly if it makes other cases worse. I'll open a small PR and canary it on dedicated-reserved cluster first.

kai: please include a small opt-out config in runtime flags: --prefer-lowregs-for-small-batch (default true for now). Also add logging: "kernel_choice_reason" = "reg_spill_detected" when we override.

sana: I'll run the microbench matrix and post results here by EOD. If we confirm, we should add a short-term regression test in CI that runs seq=32,batch=2 on p4d emulation and asserts latency within 10% of baseline.

matt: FYI, I saw a similar pattern when we tuned tile_size=128 -> 64 last quarter. Reducing tile_size improved smem reuse but increased regs because of unrolled loops. Keep an eye on compiler flags and unroll factors.

jordan: noted. Also adding a tracepoint in runtime to capture compile-time reg count for chosen kernel (parse cuobjdump) so we can make decisions without running heavy microbench in some cases.

lina: nice. One more thought — for very small batches, consider a fused single-thread kernel variant that avoids warpspecialization and uses vectorized math to reduce per-thread regs. Might be faster for batch=1 path. Low priority though.

kai: ack. I'll prepare the PR: change picker, add flag, telemetry. Jordan — can you paste the nvprof output you grabbed? I want to add counters to the trace schema.

jordan: pasted below (trimmed):
```
== Profiler results ==
Kernel: kernel_WarpSpec
reg_alloc_per_thread: 64
local_mem_spills: 3
achieved_occupancy: 0.25
shared_mem_per_cta: 12KB
inst_issued: 1.2e9

Kernel: kernel_A_lowregs
reg_alloc_per_thread: 56
local_mem_spills: 0
achieved_occupancy: 0.2
shared_mem_per_cta: 20KB
inst_issued: 1.0e9
```

sana: perfect. I'll run the matrix and attach csv. If autotuner picks lowregs for these combos, we can stable-roll in 48h.

perf-bot: Canary rollout started for flag=prefer-lowregs-for-small-batch on cluster=dedicated-us-west-2 at 2026-03-17T15:12Z. Monitoring p99/p50, regressions alert at +15%.

lina: thanks all. Action items: jordan PR (picker + telemetry + flag), kai add opt-out and doc, sana run microbench + upload results, matt add CI regression test. We'll reconvene in this thread after microbench. :rocket:
